question.worked_solution:
To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-3x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3{e}^{-3x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-3x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(-3{e}^{-3x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\int {e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-3x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3{e}^{-3x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-3x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(-3{e}^{-3x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3\int {e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I.$ We remember to add a constant of integration $C$ at the end.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3J \\ I & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3(-{e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3I) \\ I & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-9I \\ 10I & ={e}^{-3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{e}^{-3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{10}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+C\end{aligned}
$$
